text.p: Israel's Elscint Ltd expects to see significant additional revenues from faster product development after signing a development and production accord with Siemens AG, an Elscint spokeswoman said on Monday.
"I estimate that this transaction has the potential to produce trade exceeding $100 million over a five-year period," Jonathan Adereth, Elscint's CEO, said in a statement.
Under the agreement, Siemens' Medical Engineering Group and Elscint will develop and produce certain assemblies for medical-imaging systems based on computerised tomography (CT).
The two companies will continue to market their CT systems independently.
Elscint, a subsidiary of Elron Electronic Industries, also produces other medical-imaging products using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), nuclear medicine and mammography systems.
Elscint had revenues of $370.4 million the first nine months of 1996.
Siemens Medical Engineering had revenues of 7.1 billion marks in fiscal 1995/96.
